newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Anwar says property curbs necessary.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Anwar says property curbs necessary.

text.p: Malaysian Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister said on Tuesday that the government's introduction of measures to curb property sector lending were necessary to safeguard the economy.
"These measures are necessary and critical to the management of the economy," Anwar told Reuters Financial Television in an interview.
He said reaction to the measures have been "adverse", partly due also due to movements in U.S. interest rates and worries about regional markets.
Anwar, who is in Fukuoka to attend the Asian Development Bank meeting, said the government saw a possibility of asset inflation if nothing was done to curb the buoyant property market.
"The interpretation is that these are panic measures. I dispute that because we take preemptive measures early enough and we do not face a problem now. There is no glut now," Anwar said.
He said investors viewed the measures positively though there had been a temporary negative reaction.
"I think so far the investors have viewed it quite positively.

"There is a temporary transient reaction, quite negative or adverse, in the financial community, partly due to the development of interest rates in the United States and the jittery reaction to development in the region," the minister told RFTV.

Malaysia's central bank on March 28 announced that it was limiting property loans to 20 percent of a bank's outstanding loans from April 1 in an attempt to reduce exposure to what it described as the "non-productive" sector.
